transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-06 08:00 PT (15:00Z) | Duration: 58m
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jared (Redwood SE), Ravi (Redwood SE), Priya (NorthReach), Liam (NorthReach SRE), Sara (NorthReach Sec), Owen (Product)

Summary:
Brief: NorthReach is evaluating Redwood for private/VPC deployment across US and EU regions. Primary concerns: data residency, private endpoints, cross-region peering, egress restrictions, KMS integration, and whether Redwood Private can support hybrid on-prem + cloud. They want a pilot with deterministic latency and options for dedicated reserved capacity.

Topics:
- VPC peering vs Transit Gateway vs PrivateLink
- Private endpoints and NAT/egress considerations
- Region-residency (EU + US) and failover plan
- KMS/HSM and audit logs / SOC2 requirements
- Bursting to Hosted and cost tradeoffs

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): ok everyone thanks for joining, we're going to run through how Redwood Private would fit into your network. feel free to jump in any time
[00:12] Priya (NorthReach): yeah thanks, we'll mostly listen, liam will drive the infra questions. our timeline is Q3 pilot and then prod late Q4, assuming security checks pass
[00:22] Liam (NorthReach): hi hi, quick note — we cannot have inference traffic egressing to the public internet; everything has to stay within our VPCs in eu-west-1 and us-east-1, with possibility of an on-prem datacenter in the future.
[00:35] Jared (Redwood SE): got it. two quick clarifying q's. do you prefer a PrivateLink/private endpoint model, or would you consider peering/transit gateway? each has operational tradeoffs.
[00:48] Sara (Security): we prefer PrivateLink for strict egress control, but if peering gives lower latency and we can lock routes we might accept it. also encryption-at-rest with our KMS is required and we need HSM-backed keys for some data classes.
[01:05] Ravi (Redwood SE): yes re: KMS — Redwood Private supports customer-managed keys; we can integrate with AWS KMS, BYOK HSM flows, and we emit audit logs into your SIEM. i know you mentioned SOC 2 earlier?
[01:20] Priya: yeah SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 are must-haves for procurement, also SAML SSO and RBAC for console access.
[01:28] Maya: we'll share the security pack after the call.
[01:34] Owen: quick question on model hosting — do you run model inference inside our VPC or is it in your private subnet controlled by Redwood? how does traffic flow?
[01:45] Jared: good q. for Redwood Private there are two deployment patterns — agentless PrivateLink endpoints (control plane on Redwood side, data plane via VPC endpoints) or full on-prem style where you run a customer-managed data plane in your VPCs. many customers pick the hybrid: control plane in our region but inference nodes in your VPC with no public egress.
[02:03] Liam: so if we go hybrid, the GPU nodes live in our account? that helps compliance but increases ops burden for us.
[02:11] Ravi: correct. we provide an on-prem package and CloudFormation / Terraform modules for bootstrap. We also have a Dedicated model where Redwood runs nodes in a dedicated account — that's less ops on your side but it's outside your VPC and requires strict peering rules.
[02:27] Priya: latency sensitivity — we have sub-50ms SLO for simple completions in us-east for critical paths. can you meet that in a peered cross-region setup?
[02:40] Jared: sub-50ms is tight cross-region. If you provision dedicated capacity in the same AZ/region as your app (or run inference nodes in your VPC) it's achievable. Cross-region peering will add RTTs; for EU-US failover you'd likely accept higher tail latency for the failover path.
[02:58] Liam: we need guidance on IP planning. we have RFC1918 ranges in use, would like to avoid overlaps. also NAT issues — we need to ensure there is no accidental public egress for model payloads.
[03:12] Maya: we will include a sample IP plan; most customers allocate a /20 for the service subnets and we map endpoints accordingly. any overlap scenarios we handle via transit gateway route tables or PrivateLink endpoint configs.
[03:28] Priya: region gating is important — EU workloads must not be able to egress to US nodes for data residency regs. how do you enforce that?
[03:37] Ravi: policy layer — you can pin model routing to region variants, and Redwood's smart routing can be configured to enforce region constraints. for strict compliance we recommend deploying data plane nodes in each region to avoid cross-region calls.
[03:52] Owen: what's the typical network design you recommend for multi-region: multiple VPCs with peering between them, or a central transit VPC?
[04:03] Jared: many customers use a Transit Gateway for hub-and-spoke — simplifies route management and centralizes inspection. PrivateLink is used for one-off connections where you don't want to manage peering. transit gives simpler peering for many VPCs but has cost considerations.
[04:17] Sara: cost is a factor; transit gateway charges + inter-region data transfer could stack up. can Redwood quantify that?
[04:24] Maya: we can provide a cost delta table showing expected egress and peering costs under different traffic profiles — we'll need your estimated QPS and avg token sizes to model it.
[04:35] Liam: QPS: around 200 rps baseline, spikes to 1k for short peaks; token sizes average 30 tokens per request.
[04:45] Jared: thanks, that helps. caching & prefix cache could reduce tokens hitting the model significantly if you have repeated prompts. Redwood Optimize can suggest batching and prefix caching configs.
[04:58] Owen: curious about bursting — can we keep primary traffic local and burst to Redwood Hosted if demand exceeds reserved capacity?
[05:06] Ravi: yes, automatic fallback is a built-in pattern. policy can route to hosted or lower-cost variants when dedicated is saturated, with logging and fallback thresholds. However, that means data will flow outside your VPC — you'd need to accept that for burst windows or set a hard cap to avoid it.
[05:22] Sara: we probably can't allow that unless it's within a covered contract and encrypted, also we need to know which regions the hosted fallback uses.
[05:31] Maya: we can lock fallback to specific regions and provide contractual guarantees around ephemeral data retention. we'll note that in the SOW.
[05:40] Priya: monitoring & tracing — can we get per-request traces, token-level latency and cost attribution?
[05:47] Jared: yes, Redwood Console surfaces per-route token-level cost, latency histograms, and you can export traces to your tracing backend. we'll advise where to place tracing hooks depending on whether you're using private endpoints or running the data plane.
[06:00] Liam: on the networking side: if we go with transit gateway, how do you handle IP address exhaustion and announceability to our on-prem?
[06:09] Ravi: we recommend a dedicated pool and we'll coordinate BGP with your NOC during the handoff. If you plan on peering into on-prem, we'll include NAT and BGP examples in the runbook.
[06:20] Owen: HSM integration — any customers doing hardware-backed keys?
[06:24] Maya: yes, several enterprise customers use BYOK with HSM. Redwood integrates with AWS CloudHSM and can support external HSM vendors via KMIP gateways; we'll share the integration notes.
[06:36] Priya: audit logs — do they land in our S3 or do you push them? retention requirements are 7 years for some audit trails.
[06:45] Jared: we can deliver audit logs into your S3, or forward to your SIEM via Kinesis/CloudWatch subscription. retention is configurable; long-term archival to Glacier is supported.
[06:57] Liam: what's the handoff cadence with your infra team? we want a 2-week network engineering workshop, then a 4-week pilot spinup.
[07:07] Maya: we can do that. workshop + runbook then pilot. we'll block Jared and Ravi for the workshop.
[07:13] Sara: legal — we'll need DPA and a proposed IP/data flow annex before we sign anything.
[07:19] Maya: understoood, i'll send templates.
[07:24] Priya: any red flags on your side for our on-prem use-case? we're planning to host a set of GPU nodes in our colo behind the same transit fabric.
[07:34] Ravi: we support colo — customers run data plane in their co-lo, we provide the bootstrap scripts. main callouts: you need to ensure low-latency links between app and inference nodes, and we need network ACLs and security groups opened for the control plane endpoints.
[07:49] Owen: any constraints on the model sizes or quantization we can use in private mode?
[07:55] Jared: mostly dependent on the instance type you deploy. our runtime supports quantized 4-bit variants for many models to reduce memory and cost. we'll propose a mix of fp16 for large gen and quant for embeddings to hit cost targets.
[08:09] Priya: ok great. let's do a short recap and next steps.
[08:14] Maya: recap: Redwood to provide security pack + SOC docs; SEs to draft VPC peering/transit and PrivateLink options with diagrams; NorthReach to confirm strict EU/US region list and share KMS/HSM details; schedule network workshop.
[08:29] Priya: agreed. thanks everyone.
[08:33] Maya: end notes — i'll add the SOW template, and we can target the week of May 18th for the workshop.
